record.what_it_does: Hosted ecommerce platform: storefronts, catalog, orders, customers, with headless APIs.
record.auth_notes: Most REST and GraphQL Admin calls send an access token in the X-Auth-Token header. Store-level API accounts include a static access token. App-level API accounts get one token per installing store through BigCommerce's grant-code OAuth flow. Account-level API accounts have a single token owned by the parent account. Other methods: BigCommerce-generated JWTs sent as Bearer for GraphQL Storefront and B2B GraphQL, and with the PAT scheme for Payments; user-signed JWTs for Customer Login; signed payload JWTs sent to control-panel apps; and the app client ID passed as a query parameter for Current Customer. Legacy HTTP basic auth is deprecated, and new stores can't create legacy accounts. Store Management MCP uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. I removed jwt_service_account because no service-account JWT grant is documented.
record.access_notes: A developer can sign up for a 15-day free trial store with no credit card and create a store-level API account. Using a store past the trial needs a paid plan (Core from $39/mo). API limits are 20k calls/hr on Core and Growth and 60k on Scale. Partners can create sandbox stores for development in the Partner Portal, but the sandbox page doesn't state any cost or eligibility rules. An app-level OAuth app can be built in the Developer Portal without review, but as a draft it installs only on stores registered to the app owner's email. To make it installable on other merchants' stores, it must be submitted for approval, including unlisted apps.
record.api_breadth_notes: Covers catalog, orders, customers, carts, checkouts, inventory, themes, channels, pricing, metafields, payments, B2B Edition, and the Account API. Includes REST V2 and V3, plus GraphQL Storefront and Admin APIs. Well over 50 operations.
record.mcp_notes: Store Management MCP is at https://api.bigcommerce.com/mcp, with a store-scoped URL that includes the store hash. It is in early access for all stores, uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, and only the store owner can enable it. Storefront MCP gives each storefront its own URL and acts as a shopper; the store owner enables it. Community servers also exist.
record.blocker_notes: A multi-merchant OAuth toolkit needs BigCommerce approval before stores outside the developer's own email can install the app, whether it is listed or unlisted. Until then, the options are draft-app installs on the developer's own stores, or each merchant pasting a store-level API token. Both are workable as a fallback but don't scale like OAuth.
